Export a document's tables to files and a data dictionary

Source: R/export.R
grist_export.Rd

grist_export() writes each table of a document to a Parquet, CSV or JSON file in a directory, and describes the tables in a data-dict.yaml file following the data-dict specification. The result can be read by other tools, or loaded into another Grist document with grist_import().

Tables are read with convert = "auto", so dates, integers and logicals are typed. The dictionary records what Parquet files can't keep: column labels and descriptions, time zones, the choices of Choice columns, and how tables refer to each other.

Usage

grist_export(
  doc,
  to = ".",
  tables = NULL,
  format = c("parquet", "csv", "json"),
  examples = c("sample", "none"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

to

Directory to write to. It is created if it doesn't exist.

tables

Table IDs to export. NULL exports every table, including the empty Table1 that Grist puts in new documents.

format

File format for the tables: "parquet", "csv" or "json".

examples

data-dict describes the values of each column. "sample" records up to five real example values (or the range of dates) from the data. "none" leaves them empty with a todo, so no data appears in the dictionary. Columns with no values are also left empty with a todo.

overwrite

Whether to replace existing files.

Value

A data frame with one row per exported table: table, rows, columns and path, invisibly.

What the dictionary contains

  • Every table gets an id column, Grist's row ID, as its primary key.

  • A Ref column is a number(id) foreign key to the id of the table it points at, with a many-to-one relationship. RefList and Attachments columns are lists of IDs. data-dict can't declare foreign keys on lists, so no relationship is recorded for them.

  • Int and Numeric columns are both number. Formula columns are exported as values, not formulas.

  • Columns of type Any are listed by name only.

File formats

"parquet" keeps every type, including time zones and list columns, and is the default. "json" keeps numbers, logicals, missing values and list columns, and writes dates and date-times as ISO 8601 text (date-times in UTC). "csv" is plain text: list columns are written as JSON arrays, and an empty Text cell can't be told apart from a missing one.

data-dict can only point at Parquet files with source, so for CSV and JSON the dictionary has no source, and files are found by name (<table>.csv or <table>.json) next to the dictionary.

Requires the yaml12 package, and the nanoparquet package for Parquet.

See also

Other export: grist_import()

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")
grist_export(doc, "pets-export")

# Load it into another document
grist_import(grist_doc("<new doc id>"), "pets-export")
}
